agree.reason: The speech opens with traffic, which is the commissioners' stated concern, and offers the signal as a binding condition that keeps the intersection at C, which gives them a clear reason to vote yes; opposing neighbours get little beyond reassurance on parking.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the facts provided; the only slight stretches are 'the neighborhood gets the fix', which hints that traffic is solved even though 310 trips are still added, and the unsourced claim that the waiting-list households earn under 60% of median.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are mostly restated rather than worked: it misses that 72 spaces for 64 units leaves 8 spare, that 64 units would house about one in six of the 412 waiting households, and it never gives a per-hour or rush-hour breakdown of the 310 trips.

right_comparison.reason: It compares the project with an empty lot and a three-year wait, but leaves out the stronger comparison: without the project there is no signal, and Alder already backs up at 8am.

qualification.reason: Making the signal a written permit condition that keeps the intersection at C gives commissioners something they can check, but there is no timing (for example, signal installed before occupancy) and no consequence if it is missed.

objections.reason: The speech answers the traffic and parking objections, but it ignores 20 months of construction trucks on Alder and leaves out the written weekday-parking offer and the neighbour group Margaret would serve on, both of which speak directly to the opposing neighbours.

fit.reason: At roughly 400 words it is a spoken first-person statement that fits the three-minute limit and ends with a clear request.
